# Research R400 — layer-major expert upload scheduling on B570

Date: 2026-10-13 (Asia/Tokyo)

Scope: read-only source and prior-report review for the current clean parent `8b48d17c99b70d32781f9f5b056602a598a37b1c`, plus primary SYCL / Level Zero documentation. Target is Intel Arc B570 10 GiB, Ryzen 5 5600X, 128 GiB RAM, observed PCIe throughput about 6 GB/s. No source changes, build, tests, GPU work, profiler, cleanup, service or Git mutation. Only this report is new. Registry v193 in the specified clean worktree records 948 completed reports. R394v2–R399 and registry details are treated as prior evidence; this round narrows to upload overlap, source lifetime/coherence, and per-layer transfer widths. It does not revisit the known PLE / streamed-KV layer-major caveats.

## Finding

The current `Stager` already has the key lifetime mechanism needed for safe host-side lookahead: pinned host-USM ring buffers, generation-tagged worker jobs, and a per-slot event recorded after the upload. A layer-major uploader could stage one layer into a 512-slot device cache, then start staging the next layer into the same host ring while the current layer executes. The event wait before each host slot is overwritten ensures the previous H2D read has finished. This is a promising way to overlap file reads / transient GGUF blob assembly with compute, with no need for atomics shared between host and device.

The current Stager contract says `start()` is for jobs after a prior generation has finished, and its worker waits the prior `dma_done[b]` before writing a reused buffer (`src/prefill/prefill.cpp:249-405`). `issued_one()` records the H2D completion event on the copy stream and advances the issued watermark (`:367-373`). The upload caller must still wait for each job to be ready, queue the copy, then call `issued_one`; a failed copy or event is fatal to that staging generation. The safe destination/read order is: stage source bytes → enqueue H2D to the destination cache slot → record the source slot’s retirement event → wait until the whole layer’s cache writes complete → run all chunks for that layer → retire its device slots before reuse.

This overlap hides only host preparation. With a single active 512-expert device layer cache, next-layer H2D cannot target that same cache while kernels still read the current layer. Direct H2D overlap with current compute therefore needs a separate device lookahead ring and a later device-to-device copy into the layer cache, or a second full layer cache. The former adds device memory, a D2D pass and slot dependencies; the latter roughly doubles the layer-cache allocation and is unlikely to be a safe default on a 10 GiB card. Neither is guaranteed to overlap on this B570 just because SYCL exposes separate queues. Level Zero’s command-list/event APIs express dependencies, while actual simultaneous copy/compute execution is device/runtime behavior and must be measured.

The strongest first candidate is therefore a host-lookahead pipeline: upload layer L, then have the CPU prepare the jobs for L+1 while the GPU processes all prompt chunks for L. Keep H2D of L+1 behind a retirement event for L’s device cache. This can hide transient-source assembly and cold/page-cache reads, if these dominate; it cannot lower the PCIe byte count or hide the next layer’s PCIe copy. If profiling later shows a remaining upload stall large enough to justify added VRAM, a bounded device lookahead ring is the next experiment.

## Current source contracts

- `Prefill::Impl` owns `m.copy`, `stage_dev[]`, `copied[]`, `used[]`, and stage-liveness bookkeeping. The ordinary stage ring uses `MAXBLOB()`-sized slots (allocation around `src/prefill/prefill.cpp:459, 935-952`); `ring_slots(T)` sizes its slot count (around `:154-177, 1215`). R399 already established that a layer-major path can omit that ordinary ring only after every active-layer expert is resident in the separate layer cache; this report does not claim that omission as a new finding.
- `Stager::init(blob_bytes,nthreads)` allocates each host slot at the passed width using `gpu::alloc_host`; on failure it falls back to pageable vectors (`:278-294`). It does not itself guarantee all slots are pinned. Any upload schedule must report pinned and pageable cases separately and use the existing source classification / error path.
- For a `Job` with `from != nullptr`, the worker calls `ExpertSource::copy_blob` into the reusable host slot; otherwise it copies `src` bytes with `memcpy` (`:327-337`). The source interface explicitly requires this for transient GGUF blobs whose pointer does not outlive the current prompt chunk (`include/strata/core/expert_source.hpp:153-171`; implementation `src/core/expert_source.cpp:508-521, 815+`). This is the clearest CPU work a next-layer pre-stage could overlap.
- Current streaming already constructs the full ordered layer/expert sequence, marks transient and non-pinned blobs for staging, and submits each blob using its exact `lay0.blob_bytes(layer)` (`src/prefill/prefill.cpp:1568-1634`). Both inline and issuer-thread paths queue `copy_async_after` with a dependency on the previous device-slot reader, then use `copied[slot]` and Stager’s per-host-slot event (`:1620-1634, 1660-1698`). This demonstrates that event-guarded asynchronous copies are an existing pattern; it does not prove a new layer-cache upload path is correct.
- The runtime’s `gpu::alloc_host` is `sycl::malloc_host(bytes, rt().context())` (`src/core/gpu.cpp:147-155`), and `gpu::copy_async_after` submits a SYCL handler memcpy with an optional event dependency and assigns the returned event as the completion event (`:271-285`). The Khronos SYCL 2020 spec requires memcpy host pointers or accessible same-context USM pointers; queue memcpy returns an event. The event is the portable completion boundary for source reuse. Level Zero describes explicit command-list dependencies/events; independent command lists do not imply cross-list order by themselves.
- `ExpertLayout::blob_bytes(layer)` is constant for non-native packs and layer-specific for native packs; `max_blob` is the largest layer size (`include/strata/kernels/cpu/expert_layout.hpp:21-42`). `ExpertCache::fill_slot` queues only the requested byte count when `bytes > 0 && bytes <= blob_`, otherwise uses the slot size (`src/core/expert_cache.cpp:583-603`). Thus passing exact layer bytes already avoids transferring slot padding. The legacy `open(n_slots,...,blob_bytes)` allocates uniform slots; `open_sized` gives slots separate 256-byte-rounded extents (`include/strata/core/expert_cache.hpp:95-107, 180-220`; implementation `src/core/expert_cache.cpp:475-535`). Exact slot widths save allocation slack when layer sizes vary, not H2D bytes if callers already pass exact lengths.
- `fill_slot` is asynchronous and does not establish a cache residency publication fence (`src/core/expert_cache.cpp:583-603`). A new layer-major owner must not make a layer runnable until all its slot-fill events have completed successfully. It must drain users of the cache before overwriting or freeing slots. This is a source ownership and ordering requirement, not a claim about a current implementation.

## Transfer arithmetic and measured anchors

Historical PR #6 measured 50.292 GB of expert traffic for the layer-major 32K prompt versus 190.110 GB for the chunk-major baseline, with the paired quiet-wall medians 645.848 versus 453.2935 prefill tok/s. R394v2/R395v2 preserve the exact recipe, all-head/output matching and limitations: IQ3_S, B570, 5600X, 128 GiB RAM, 32,768 input tokens, 8K chunks, 65,538 context, all K/V resident, no trace timers, old source commit `f263d87d44aa671d056c33e6c6b6b0635fc25b8c`. See [PR #6 pinned run artifacts](https://github.com/yqYo1/Strata/tree/d0c5dda0dc2e8d82458c4b0ff31c4cef44c40b32/bench/results/2026-10-05-sycl-prefill-scaling/layer-major).

Static floor arithmetic at the user-provided observed 6 GB/s is:
- 50.292 GB / 6 GB/s ≈ 8.38 s for the layer-major recorded expert bytes.
- 190.110 GB / 6 GB/s ≈ 31.69 s for the recorded baseline bytes.
- Difference ≈ 23.30 s of ideal transfer time.

These are decimal-byte lower-bound estimates only. They assume a sustained 6 GB/s in the relevant direction with no submission, page fault, host staging, synchronization or contention cost. They are not measured upload times and cannot be subtracted from the historical wall times as a causal decomposition. The historical 21.55 s median wall reduction is close in scale, which supports retaining transfer scheduling as a strong candidate; it does not establish that all measured gain came from transfer.

The current per-blob streaming copy already uses exact layer width, so an exact-width cache layout cannot cut the 50.292 GB historical payload unless it changes which blobs are moved or how often. At 6 GB/s, useful rate gains must come from lower repeated traffic, overlapping a serialized stage, or improving CPU/file-source preparation—not from excluding unused bytes beyond each blob.

## Prioritized candidates

1. **Host-side next-layer preparation (best first experiment).** After all 512 current-layer cache uploads have been enqueued, launch the next Stager generation to read/assemble next-layer jobs into its host ring while current-layer chunks run. Do not submit these next-layer blobs into the active layer cache. Per-buffer `dma_done` events serialize host-slot overwrite against the earlier layer’s H2D source read. Start current layer compute only after its 512 cache-fill completion events are checked. At the layer boundary, submit next-layer H2D and wait for its completion before any expert kernel reads it. This adds no new GPU buffer and uses the current mapped host-ring API. Keep a strict bound on lookahead (one layer) and stop/join workers on all failure/cancel paths using the existing drain order.
2. **Source-class-specific staging.** For immutable pinned arena/mmap blobs, staging does only a copy of the pointer into the pinned ring and may cost more than direct copy; retain direct H2D where the source is explicitly DMA-safe and stable. For transient GGUF assembly or an unpinned/read path, host lookahead may remove CPU work from the GPU-critical path. Track bytes and elapsed host preparation by source class; do not infer a win from `pinned()` alone.
3. **Conditional device lookahead ring.** Only if the first experiment leaves a material PCIe wait: add a small separate device ring sized in complete experts, populate it for layer L+1 during compute of L, then enqueue D2D from ring to L’s layer-cache slot after current-layer readers retire. Carry one event per device-ring slot and explicit layer/expert/generation identity; never publish the target slot before D2D completion. Compare 4/8/16 slots; compute exact VRAM cost as slots × actual maximum blob width. Reject if D2D traffic and the extra synchronization erase overlap or consume required headroom.
4. **Exact-sized cache allocation (capacity-only).** For native packs with varying layer widths, `open_sized` or a per-layer exact allocation can reclaim padding from currently over-wide uniform slots. This is peak-live-byte/headroom optimization only: peak allocation still needs 512 × largest layer blob, and repeated per-layer allocation may fragment or add startup latency. It cannot reduce transferred bytes when `fill_slot` receives exact widths. Keep separate from throughput claims.
5. **Bulk contiguous layer copy (conditional source API).** Arena-backed expert packs may store a layer’s 512 blobs contiguously, but the current `ExpertSource` abstraction exposes per-expert blobs, not a checked contiguous-layer view. A single bulk H2D could reduce submission count but requires a source capability that proves contiguity, immutability and exact extent; it does not apply automatically to GGUF shards/transient blobs. Measure submission overhead before adding such an API.

## Required qualification before promoting

The first comparison should isolate the 32K historical recipe and preserve its old status. Use three alternating pairs on the same binary for default current route versus host-lookahead layer-major; exact same 32,768-token fixture, context/KV policy, chunk, cache, PLE/source settings, input/output horizon, process warmup and timer boundaries as PR #6. Record every arm’s prefill wall, output token and complete first head; retain source/build/runtime identities. Report separately pinned-direct, pinned-staged, pageable fallback and transient-source counts/bytes/time. Measure from source request through successful device completion, not just enqueue time. Keep all phase/transfer diagnostics off for the wall run; use a separate diagnostic run for per-stage timings.

Also qualify:
- repeated copy/compute queue event ordering and the forced-drain path on cancel, injected copy failure and Stager failure; do not free source/cache/ring memory until both queues and producer threads are retired;
- exact 512 slot-to-expert mapping, per-layer native blob width, bytes copied, slot contents and successful completion before the first expert read; output-head equality alone cannot establish cache identity;
- whether host lookahead is still useful with fully resident mmap/arena sources and warm OS cache; separate this from the transient GGUF/sharded case;
- B570 actual concurrent compute/H2D behavior before trying the device ring; Level Zero/SYCL permits expressing async commands and dependencies but makes no guarantee that independent work overlaps on this exact device/driver;
- fresh free VRAM and host pinned-memory budget with decode cache, head, active session, workspace and runtime owners present; no fit guarantee follows from nominal 10 GiB or 128 GiB;
- only after a stable matched wall result, repeat at 64K with the exact PR #8 prompt/chunk and unchanged K/V/cache policy. Preserve the historical 64K samples as instrumented single runs, not medians (see R394v2 and [PR #8 artifacts](https://github.com/yqYo1/Strata/tree/dd0f6e782e5a0ac3dab46ccd56ed711a4f1d5153/bench/results/2026-10-05-sycl-prefill-scaling/cache-release)).

## Primary references

- Khronos, [SYCL 2020 Specification revision 12](https://registry.khronos.org/SYCL/specs/sycl-2020/html/sycl-2020.html): USM pointer/accessibility and explicit memory operations. Use queue/handler event dependencies for asynchronous copies and completion.
- Intel, [Level Zero Core Programming Guide / API](https://oneapi-src.github.io/level-zero-spec/level-zero/latest/core/api.html): command queues, command lists, events and memory-copy APIs. Cross-list dependencies need explicit event/wait edges; merely using different queues is not a completion guarantee.
- Intel oneAPI DPC++ compiler, [SYCL environment variables and Level Zero event behavior](https://intel.github.io/llvm/EnvironmentVariables.html): implementation controls can affect event behavior; not a performance guarantee.
- Current source: `src/prefill/prefill.cpp:249-405, 459, 935-952, 1568-1698`; `src/core/gpu.cpp:147-155, 271-285`; `src/core/expert_cache.cpp:475-535, 583-603`; `include/strata/core/expert_source.hpp:153-171`; `include/strata/kernels/cpu/expert_layout.hpp:21-42`.
- Prior retained evidence: `research-historical-performance-regression-round394-v2.txt`, `research-upstream-inference-merge-regression-round395-v2.txt`, `research-layer-major-current-lifetime-round396-v1.txt`, `research-layer-major-kv-capacity-round397-v1.txt`, `research-layer-major-streamed-existing-path-round398-v1.txt`, and `research-layer-major-compact-workspace-parity-round399-v1.txt` under `/home/yayoi/.local/state/strata-sycl/post-reboot-tuning-20261007/research-20261009/`.

Evidence limits: This report proposes no code or schedule change and makes no measured claim about host-lookahead usefulness, concurrent copy/compute, 6 GB/s being sustained for cache uploads, source correctness under mutation, or VRAM fit. The current Stager is a reusable primitive, not proof that the proposed layer cache lifecycle has been implemented. The 6 GB/s arithmetic is a floor estimate; only a matched, repeated run can establish wall benefit.
